plans.note: Cap is mutual at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with Excluded Claims in 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, IP infringement) and 21.4 anti-severance language. Check 21.2 does not exclude data-restoration/replacement costs (it expressly makes them direct). Also cross-check Section 19.5 disclaimer and 18.2 (insurance does not limit liability).

No Section 20 indemnity clause appears in the outline even though Section 9.3 cross-references 'Section 20.5' remedies and 21.3/30.5 assume indemnification obligations and indemnified parties. Likely a missing Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity; confirm no indemnity text sits elsewhere before marking missing.

Section 12.4 (second instance) bars Customer from developing, marketing, selling or acquiring competing products for the term plus 24 months in any territory — a direct restraint on our business and walk-away territory. Note the conflict with Section 12.3, which states Customer made no non-compete commitment.

Section 12.3 preserves our freedom to engage any supplier, but check Section 7.2 (first instance, match-or-disclose before engaging another provider) and Section 2.1 take-or-pay for de facto exclusivity; primary exclusivity analysis rests on 12.3 unless 7.2 is read as a sourcing restraint (which is better handled under MFN).

Section 7.2 (first instance) requires Customer to disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer before engaging another provider — an MFN running against us, contradicting 12.3's statement that no most-favoured-customer commitment was made. Do not double-flag the same term under EXCLUSIVITY.

Section 12.4 (first instance) bars soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee for the term plus 24 months with no general-advertising or responding-applicant carve-out ('regardless of how the employee applies'); conflicts with the general-recruitment freedom in 12.3.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency and security/SLA/legal-violation termination rights (9.1–9.3) plus 9.5; no Customer termination for convenience appears, and Section 2.1 expressly denies reduction or termination rights. Check 8.2 non-renewal and 27.3 force-majeure exit as partial substitutes before concluding the convenience right is missing.

Section 8.2 gives 12-month renewals with only 30 days' notice of non-renewal plus a 60-day Vendor reminder and deadline extension; Section 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Likely compliant/at-preferred; note any minor gaps in the rationale rather than redlining.

Section 28.1 imposes Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list — and directly conflicts with 28.2's exclusive New York County venue. Resolve to an accepted law/venue; 28.3 escalation is acceptable.

24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and change of control; 24.4 bars Vendor termination or repricing on our change of control. Cross-check 13.3 licence transferability. Likely compliant.

Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence — contrary to our owning what we pay for. Customer Data ownership in 14.1 is fine; note tension with 13.2/14.3 perpetual licence and 10.1/10.2 delivery of Deliverables.

13.1 covers Affiliates and contractors; 13.2 grants a perpetual paid-up licence; 13.3 limits revocation to material uncured breach with cure. The revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence in 14.2 is the conflict — flag it under IP and cite it here rather than double-flagging.

22.1 limits audits to once per 12 months with 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality; 22.2 puts costs on Vendor absent >5% underpayment and bars system/data access; 22.3 makes findings our Confidential Information. Likely compliant.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer is evident; 7.3 bars interest on amounts not due and 27.3 allows termination without penalty. Check 2.1 take-or-pay (handled under MINCOMMIT) and 22.2 shortfall/audit-cost shifting, which is a cost recovery rather than a penalty.

19.1–19.3 give professional-services, conformance, legal-compliance and malicious-code warranties; 19.2 gives 90 days for Deliverables and full-term conformance for hosted Services; 19.4 provides re-perform/repair/replace with refund and termination fallback and is non-exclusive. Likely compliant.

18.1 sets CGL 1M/2M, workers' comp, employer's liability 1M, E&O 2M and cyber 5M for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers insurer quality, certificates, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. Assess adequacy of limits given health data, but likely compliant.

Section 2.1 imposes USD 2,000,000 per year for three years on a take-or-pay basis expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — no exit, walk-away territory; note the contradiction with 12.3's no-minimum-volume statement and the absence of a convenience termination right.

Section 10 addresses access wind-down, Deliverable delivery and refunds, and 16.5 covers return/destruction of Confidential Information, but no express Customer Data export in a usable format or transition-assistance/exit-services obligation appears (Sections 11 and 23 referenced but with no visible text). Verify before marking missing.
